reasoning: Skeptic lane. Filings carry most of the bear case: the 10-K says well over half of LEU deliveries come from TENEX and other sources are 'not sufficient to replace' it; waivers for 2026-27 are still pending and the ban leaves no waivers after 2027; Q2 SWU price +3% vs unit cost +13%; HALEU operation contract unfunded; two convert issues ($1.2B, cash principal) and a $500M equity+warrant raise in September despite $1.87B of cash; 10-Q flags large follow-on offerings. Sell-side has been cutting (UBS $170 on hiring costs, Needham $262->$206 on 2026-10-20, Jefferies Hold $169, Guggenheim $167 as a recent underwriter); short interest 30%. No open-market insider selling found (Form 4s are tax withholding), no litigation of size beyond legacy Piketon release suits. Valuation: the business is a fading resale franchise plus net cash (~$19/share at horizon after capex) plus a first-of-a-kind build whose economics at $200/SWU and ~$1,000/SWU of capacity are close to zero NPV at a 10% rate; today's price needs ~0.8 success odds. Methods: engine DCF/multiple with rNPV adjustment ($26-33), market-share states ($52), cash floor + option ($67) -> fair value ~$44. Ladder: market price has beaten models as a 12-month forecast, so I centre at ~$80 (geometric blend of $110 and ~$50), sigma ~0.75 from 89% realised vol, slightly fatter right tail for squeeze/policy; P(>= $110) 0.335. model_inputs.structure_note: Method-fit flagged LEU (EBITDA margin 3.6% TTM; net cash 29% of market cap): standard multiples do not value it. The value is carried by (1) net cash at the horizon (balance.net_debt_horizon -490) and Westerman at its purchase price (adjustment +116); (2) the Piketon LEU/HALEU expansion as an rNPV 'adjustment' (phases 0.70 x 0.75, peak revenue $900M, cash margin 55%, net post-horizon spend after DOE task-order cash entered as dev_costs), added on top of the core legs; (3) two custom legs: market-share scenarios (method b, $52.1) and cash floor + expansion option (method e, $67.4). The years model only the CORE business (SWU/uranium resale + residual Technical Solutions) with maintenance capex, because expansion capex and pre-operating cost sit in the rNPV dev_costs and in net_debt_horizon; FY2028 is the first year without Russian supply for US customers, so the core fades - that is the economics, not a modelling trough to fix. The engine DCF (0.40) and EV/EBITDA (0.10) legs are therefore core + rNPV + net cash.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (a) expansion economics are unpublished (company says only 'multi-billion'); I use $3.6B gross programme capex (~$0.9B by the horizon, $2.7B after) for ~3.5M SWU + 12 MTU HALEU, net of the $900M DOE task order; +/-$1B on capex moves fair value by about +/-$25/share. (b) Success probability 0.525 from US base rates (USEC's American Centrifuge Project suspended, AREVA Eagle Rock cancelled, GLE Paducah unbuilt; only Urenco USA built) lifted for $3.4B of appropriations and the Russian ban. (c) Net cash at horizon -490 is derived (see inputs_detail), not reported; the Q3 2026 10-Q (due ~2026-11-04) will reset it. (d) Expected equity raise (~$475M at ~$105, p 0.5) is in both shares.horizon and net_debt_horizon. (e) Deferred tax assets/NOLs not valued (small). Fair value = engine base horizon value; the price ladder deliberately sits above it (median ~$80) because the market price has beaten every model blend as a 12-month forecast. Versus consensus: StockAnalysis forward P/E 40.82 at $109.88 implies NTM EPS ~$2.69; my FY2027 GAAP EPS is ~$0.15 (core EBIT 64 + net interest ~30 - expensed expansion pre-op ~90, taxed, / ~24M shares), >90% below, because pre-operating build cost is expensed, the LEU margin keeps compressing and street EPS is largely adjusted. My core revenue (FY2027 $415M) excludes Westerman (~$150M external, carried at purchase price) and $900M task-order revenue (carried as a cash offset in the rNPV), so it is not comparable to street revenue.
